title: Missing Values & Outliers
html:
Real data has gaps and extreme values. Handle them deliberately: understand why a value is missing or extreme, then choose a strategy — and fit that strategy on the training data only.

Why values go missing

MechanismMeaningExampleConsequence
MCAR — missing completely at randomMissingness unrelated to anythingA sensor randomly drops packetsDropping rows loses data but doesn't bias
MAR — missing at randomDepends on observed columnsOlder users skip the income question more oftenImpute using the other columns
MNAR — missing not at randomDepends on the missing value itselfHigh earners hide their incomeMissingness is informative — add an indicator

Strategies

StrategyWhenCaveat
Drop rowsFew rows affected, MCARThrows data away; can bias if not MCAR
Drop columnMostly empty and uninformativeCheck first whether missingness predicts the target
Mean / median / most-frequent / constantQuick baseline (SimpleImputer)Shrinks variance; median is robust to outliers
Missing-indicator columnMissingness may carry signaladd_indicator=True
KNN / iterative imputationFeatures are related to each otherSlower; still fit on train only
Native supportHistGradientBoosting*, scikit-learn trees (≥ 1.3), XGBoost, LightGBMThe model learns where missing values should go
Watch out

Computing the imputation value on the full dataset before splitting leaks test information into training. Put imputers inside a Pipeline so each cross-validation fold fits its own.

Outliers: detect

IQR rule: outlier if x < Q1 − 1.5·IQR or x > Q3 + 1.5·IQR z-score rule: |x − mean| / std > 3

The z-score rule assumes roughly normal data and is distorted by the very outliers it looks for (masking); median/IQR-based rules are more robust. For many features at once use a model-based detector such as Isolation Forest (see Anomaly Detection).

Outliers: decide

Kind of outlierAction
Data error (age 250, negative price)Fix or set to missing
Real but rare (a genuine 250k salary)Keep; reduce its leverage with a log transform, capping, or a robust model/loss
The thing you want to find (fraud)Definitely keep — it's the signal
  • Tree-based models split on thresholds, so extreme feature values barely affect them.
  • Linear models, k-NN, k-means and anything using means or squared errors are sensitive to them.
  • Robust choices: median instead of mean, RobustScaler, MAE or Huber loss instead of MSE.
Mean or median imputation?

Median for skewed features or when outliers are present — the mean is pulled toward extreme values. Either way, add a missing indicator when missingness may carry information, and compare against a model that handles NaN natively.

Should you remove outliers?

Only if they are errors. Real extreme values are information — removing them makes the model overconfident on exactly the cases that matter. Prefer transformation, capping or robust methods, and never remove outliers from the test set to make scores look better.
